subject: Harmonize term boundary + accelerate capacity ahead of renewal
messages:
From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@lumenedge.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@lumenedge.com
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal timing + surge ahead of contract

Hi Tessa —

Quick note as we head into the May renewal window: our traffic pattern changed after the Q1 product launch and we’ve already consumed ~40% more tokens than forecasted. We have the contract renewal (current term ends 2027-07-31) coming up and need to do two things before the renewal:

1) Harmonize our renewal with a new fiscal calendar (we want to move to a 2028-01-31 boundary instead of July).
2) Get additional capacity immediately to cover expected Q3 demand spike — ideally a short-term burst or a frontloaded uplift in committed capacity.

Can you share options that preserve unit pricing but give us runway? Procurement would prefer a single amendment rather than multiple addenda. I’ve attached Q1 usage for context.

Appreciate a short list of practical paths and any documentation procurement needs.

—Sarah
Sarah Park
Head of Platform Operations, LumenEdge
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@lumenedge.com>
Cc: priyom.das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, david.kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + surge ahead of contract

Hi Sarah — thanks for the context and the file.

We can absolutely help and aim to keep your effective unit economics steady. High-level options we typically recommend; I’ve asked our pricing lead (Priyom) to sketch numbers and procurement docs:

A) Short-term bridge + co-term amendment
   - 3-month bridge increase (burst capacity) added to current term with credits applied to next period; no change to base CPI.
   - Amendment to co-term the contract to 2028-01-31 in the same doc so procurement has one signature flow.

B) Frontloaded annual commit with graduated ramp (preferred for scale)
   - Convert to a 12-month accelerated annual commitment starting immediately; frontloaded portion covers Q3 surge, then monthly ramp-down of reserved capacity to baseline.
   - Preserves per-token price with a 6% uplift for the frontload credit structure (laid out in pricing grid).

C) Multi-year tiered deal with capacity escrow
   - 24-month term, tiered commit with automatic annual step-ups; includes an early-burst allowance and defined true-up windows.

Next steps: Priyom will send a side-by-side schedule + a short draft amendment for procurement to review. If helpful we can run a 30-minute call with procurement and finance to confirm cashflow/tax preferences.

Which option would you like us to prioritize for a formal draft?

Best,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: priyom.das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Sarah Park <sarah.park@lumenedge.com>
Cc: david.kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal timing + surge ahead of contract — option details + draft

Sarah / Tessa — attaching a short package: 1) pricing-schedule-optionB.xlsx (frontload + ramp math), 2) Renewal_Amendment_draft_v1.pdf (single amendment to co-term + bridge language). I pulled estimated monthly token volumes from the Q1 file and modeled three paths. Highlights below: 

- Option A (Bridge + co-term): Immediate 200k token burst for 3 months; credit applied as a one-time invoice credit equal to 85% of overage cost, then co-term to 2028-01-31. Estimated incremental spend vs run-rate: +$27k over 3 months, but full credit lowers net cash to ~$4k.

- Option B (Frontloaded annual commit): Upfront commitment covering next 9 months at 1.0x baseline + 30% frontload; unit price unchanged, we apply a 6% effective discount by amortizing credits across 12 months. Net present cash flow is more favorable for LumenEdge and requires a single signature.

- Option C (24mo tiered): Best for predictable growth; requires procurement sign-off on early exit terms.

Procurement docs included: one-page SOW summary in the PDF and a marked amendment. I also attached LumenEdge_Q1_usage.csv with the raw numbers.

If you confirm Option B, I’ll prepare a redlined amendment (legal-friendly) and route for signature via DocuSign. If procurement prefers minimal paperwork, Option A will get you immediate capacity today and we can follow with the co-terming amendment.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Principal Pricing Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: pricing-schedule-optionB.xlsx; Renewal_Amendment_draft_v1.pdf; LumenEdge_Q1_usage.csv
From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@lumenedge.com>
To: priyom.das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@lumenedge.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + surge ahead of contract — option details + draft

Team — thanks, that package is exactly what procurement needed. We’ll proceed with Option B (Frontloaded annual commit). A couple quick asks before we route: 

• Can you produce one redline that folds the co-term to 2028-01-31 and shows the amortized credit math by month?
• Procurement wants the amendment as a single DocuSign envelope and a separate invoice schedule showing the upfront amount + amortization.

If you can get the redline and DocuSign ready by EOD Friday (14 May), procurement will sign and I’ll confirm internal budget.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — this keeps our quarter deliverables aligned.

—Sarah
Sarah Park
Head of Platform Operations, LumenEdge
Procurement: procurement@lumenedge.com
